threads.body: This comment references `LettuceReactiveCommandInstrumentation`, but no such class exists. The class that actually consumes `COMMAND_CONTEXT_KEY` in the reactive flow is `LettuceObservableCommandInstrumentation`. The reference should be corrected to avoid misleading future maintainers (compare with the accurate reference in `LettuceAsyncCommandsInstrumentation`, which points to `LettuceAsyncCommandInstrumentation`).

For naming consistency, consider prefixing this class with `Lettuce` (e.g. `LettuceReactiveCommandDispatcherInstrumentation`). Every other `TypeInstrumentation` in this module and the lettuce-5.0 module uses the `Lettuce` prefix (`LettuceAsyncCommandInstrumentation`, `LettuceAsyncCommandsInstrumentation`, `LettuceConnectInstrumentation`, and the sibling class added in this PR, `LettuceObservableCommandInstrumentation`), so this class is the lone outlier. Renaming would also require renaming the file and updating the reference in `LettuceInstrumentationModule`.

This `isCompletedWithValue` check runs as a one-shot assertion right after `waitAndAssertTraces` returns. The GET span is ended in `LettuceObservableCommandInstrumentation.TerminalAdvice.onEnter`, i.e. before the `complete()` body that emits the value and runs `future::complete`. As a result, `waitAndAssertTraces` can observe all three spans and return before the subscriber has completed the future, so this assertion is racy. The sibling `LettuceAsyncClientTest` wraps the same kind of check in `await().untilAsserted(...)` (e.g. `LettuceAsyncClientTest.java:220`) to avoid this; consider doing the same here (this also requires importing `org.awaitility.Awaitility.await`).

Same race as in `testAsyncSubscriber`: the GET span is recorded in the terminal advice's `onEnter` before the subscriber callback runs `future::complete`, so `waitAndAssertTraces` can return before the future is completed and this one-shot `isCompletedWithValue` assertion may fail intermittently. With `subscribeOn(Schedulers.io())` the callback also runs on a separate thread, widening the window. Wrap it in `await().untilAsserted(...)` to match the convention used in `LettuceAsyncClientTest`.
